Cnr No Dlse01-004078-2019 Kailash Kumar S/o Late Bharat Singh R/o 548, Gali no. 16, J- 1st, Sangam Vihar, New Delhi. .....Claimant/ Versus Saurabh Singhal S/o Sh. N.K. Singhal R/o 1598, Bhagwan Gali, Saini Basti K. M. Pur, New Delhi. ............Driver/Resp Rajesh Gupta S/o Late Sh. Lakhan Lal Gupta R/o A-1407/1, Wazir Nagar, K.M. Pur New Delhi.
texts.facts: In this case, a detailed accident report was filed by police in terms of provisions of Motor Vehicle Act and same is treated as Claim Petition in view of the provisions contained in such Act. 2. Brief facts of the case are that on 09.05.2019 at about 07.30 AM, petitioner was crossing the road at Kotla Red Light near Arya Samaj Mandir, B. P. Marg, New Delhi, all of sudden Ecco Car bearing no. DL 1CR 8686 which was being driven by its driver in very rash and negligent manner, came from Jawahar Lal Nehru Stadium side and hit him while taking turn towards Kotla. Due to said he fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries in his right leg and other injuries on all over his body. 3. He was immediately taken to JPN Apex Trauma Center, AIIMS, New Delhi where the doctors of the said hospital have declared grievous injuries in his right leg and other injuries on all over his body. He was further treated by the doctors of the above said hospital till 07.08.2021. 4. The police after investigation, in FIR No. 155/19 PS K. M. Pur filed charge sheet u/s 279/337/338 IPC and 146/196 MV Act. DAR was also filed by the investigating officer. 5. At this stage, it may be noted that this is a case without insurance, of the offending vehicle in question at the relevant time. therefore, my Ld. Predecessor directed the respondents, in view of judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, Jai Prakash vs M/S. National Insurance Co. & Ors on 17 MACT No.435/19 Kailash Kumar Vs. Saurabh Singhal & Ors. Page No . 2 of 21 BK December, 2009 to deposit security in the FORM of FDR of Rs. 2.5 lakhs to satisfy the award that may be ultimately passed. Further, directions were given vide order dated 11.12.2019 to get the vehicle auctioned and send the proceed thereof to this Tribunal. 6. As per record, respondent failed to make such deposit, as such, as per order dated 11.10.2019, my Ld. Predecessor closed the right to file reply. Accordingly, they were further not allowed to cross examine the petitioner side witness. 7. From the material on record, the following issues were framed on 11.12.2019 by my Ld. Predecessor: 1. OPP 2. 8. Petitioner Kailash Kumar, filed his examination in chief by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. He relied upon his Aadhar Card as Ex.PW1/1, PAN card as Ex.PW1/2, Salary certificate for the month of April 2019 as Ex.PW1/3, MLC as Ex.PW1/4, Kailash Kumar vs . Saurabh Singhal & Ors. on 16 September, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22407651/ 2 original discharge summary with OPD cards as Ex.PW1/5 (colly), original medical bills amounting of Rs. 13,346/- as Ex.PW1/6 (colly) and DAR as Ex.PW1/7. 9. No other evidence has been led on behalf of petitioner. 10. No evidence was allowed to be led on behalf of respondents. 11. Further petitioner applied for disability certificate and a disability certificate dated 12.04.2022 from Pt. Madan Mohan Malviya Hospital, Delhi was received in which 33% permanent disability relating to right lower limb MACT No.435/19 Kailash Kumar Vs. Saurabh Singhal & Ors. Page No. 3 of 21 BK was given. Further, he also filed written arguments in form VIB. It has been further held that the proceedings under the Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to the proceedings in a Civil Suit and hence, strict rules of evidence are not applicable. 16. In the present case, police after investigation had filed charge-sheet against respondent no.1 under section 279/338 of IPC which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent in causing the accident. The IO has filed Detailed Accident Report before this Tribunal. 17. In his examination in chief PW-1/ Victim/ Injured / Petitioner deposed that on 09.05.2019 at about 07:30 AM, he was crossing the road near Arya Samaj Mandir, B. P. Marg, New Delhi, suddently, offending vehicle / Eeco Car, driven by R-1/ Saurabh Kailash Kumar vs . Saurabh Singhal & Ors. on 16 September, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22407651/ 3 Singhal in a very rash and negligent manner came from jawahar Lal Nehru statdium and hit PW-1 while taking turn towards Kotla. As a result of which he failed on road and sustained grievous injuries on his right leg and other injuries to whole of the body. He further deposed that he was taken to AIIMS Trauma Centre for his medical treatment. It was further deposed that due to rash and negligent driving of the R-1, the accident in question took place, he further deposed that he was treated at Madan Mohan Malviya Hospital, New Delhi till 07.08.2021. 18. That he was working as office attendant/ conductor with Delhi-Kannada Education Society (regd) at Lodhi Estate, New Delhi and was getting a salary of Rs. 19136/- per month. As per record, petitioner is residing in MACT No.435/19 Kailash Kumar Vs. Saurabh Singhal & Ors. (iii) Expenditure on special diet : Rs.20,000/- There is no prescription for special diet. The nature of injuries are grievous and petitioner suffered 33% permanent physical impairment in relation to his right lower limb. Further, it is held that due to such accident, he suffered monetary loss in the form of loss of E.L. for about 100 days. The Rs.50,000/- petitioner has suffered grievous injuries and suffered 33% permanent physical impairment in relation to his right lower limb.
texts.arguments: 15. In Bimla Devi & Ors vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & ors [(2009) 13 SC 530,[ in Kaushnumma Begum and others v/s New India Assurance Company Limited, [2001 ACJ 421 SC[, in National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana cited as [2009 ACJ 287], it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view is to be taken. In National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet u/s 279/338 IPC are sufficient proof of negligence of MACT No.435/19 Kailash Kumar Vs. Saurabh Singhal & Ors. Page No. 4 of 21 BK the driver of the offending vehicle. At this stage, before proceeding further, by rely upon the judgments of C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair, R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. and Baker v. Willoughby which are referred and relied in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343 decided by Hon'ble SC, it can be noted that the provision of the Motor MACT No.435/19 Kailash Kumar Vs. Saurabh Singhal & Ors. Page No. 5 of 21 BK Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. 20.6. It was observed by Hon'ble Sc in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability--Item (ii) (a). It is further argued by learned counsel for petitioner that in any case he suffered opportunity cost of more than three month, as otherwise he would have got benefit of such earned leave. On the other hand, it is stated by counsel for insurance company that no such monetary loss is suffered by such person and he continued to get his salary MACT No.435/19 (iii) Percentage of loss of earning Nil capacity in relation to disability: 1. In view of judgment of Raj Kumar(supra), it can be noted that in the present case petitioner suffered 33% physical impairment in relation to his right lower limb. 3.Further in such case of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar, the Hon'ble Supreme Court laid down a three step approach to decide compensation for the injured persons who have suffered permanent disability and same are as under: i) Tribunal should see as to what the injured can do inspite of permanent disability and what the injured cannot do: 32. At this stage, it is relevant to the refer to the judgment of A. V. Padma & Ors. Vs., R. Venugopal & Ors. (2012) 3 Supreme Court Cases 378: " ......In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". But if the Tribunal is satisfied for reasons to be stated in writing that the whole or part of the amount is required for expanding an existing business or for purchasing some property for earning a livelihood, the Tribunal can release the whole or part of the amount of compensation to the claimant provided the Tribunal will ensure that the amount is invested for the purpose for which MACT No.435/19 Kailash Kumar Vs. Saurabh Singhal & Ors. Page No. 16 of 21 BK it is demanded and paid. Moreover, in the case of literate persons, the Tribunal may resort to the procedure indicated in guideline No. (i) only if, having regard to the age, fiscal background and strata of the society to which the claimant belongs Kailash Kumar vs . Saurabh Singhal & Ors. on 16 September, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22407651/ 11 and such other considerations, the Tribunal thinks that in the larger interest of the claimant and with a view to ensure the safety of the compensation awarded, it is necessary to invest the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit.
